title: Restatement Practice: Daily Choices
instructions: Choose the option that best restates the meaning of the original sentence.

content.intro: Read each original sentence carefully. Choose the option with the closest meaning.

questions.stem: Because the library becomes crowded after lunch, students who need a quiet desk should arrive earlier.

options.A: Students are not allowed to enter the library after lunch.
options.B: Arriving before lunchtime gives students a better chance of finding a quiet desk.
options.C: The library provides quieter desks to students who stay all day.
options.D: Students should leave their desks when the library becomes crowded.

questions.rationale: Both sentences express that earlier arrival improves the chance of finding quiet space.

questions.stem: The event will take place outdoors unless the weather conditions become unsafe.

options.A: The event will move indoors only if the weather creates a risk.
options.B: The event was cancelled because the outdoor area was unsafe.
options.C: The organisers prefer unsafe weather to an indoor event.
options.D: The weather must improve before the event can be planned.

questions.rationale: Unless introduces the only condition that would prevent the outdoor plan.

questions.stem: Mina did not realise how useful the workshop had been until she started her first project.

options.A: Mina began the project before attending the workshop.
options.B: The workshop became less useful when Mina started working.
options.C: Starting a real project made Mina understand the value of the workshop.
options.D: Mina only attended the workshop because her project had failed.

questions.rationale: Her later project experience revealed the workshop's usefulness.

questions.stem: Although the new bus route is longer, it is more reliable during the morning rush hour.

options.A: The shorter bus route is always more reliable in the morning.
options.B: The new route takes more distance but is less likely to be delayed in busy morning traffic.
options.C: Morning passengers refuse to use the route because it is unreliable.
options.D: The new route is both shorter and faster during every part of the day.

questions.rationale: The contrast between greater length and better reliability is preserved.

questions.stem: Students are encouraged to ask for feedback before submitting the final version of their report.

options.A: Students should consider getting comments while they can still revise the report.
options.B: Only the final version of a report can receive feedback.
options.C: Students must submit the report before asking any questions.
options.D: Feedback is unnecessary when a report has several versions.

questions.rationale: Both sentences recommend feedback before the final submission, while revision remains possible.
